definition: Agrarian means relating to farming, cultivated land, or a society built around it.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word agrarian. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know agrarian should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The saga opens in an agrarian province where the whole year turns on plowing, sowing, and the state of the wheat.

Rural is weaker than agrarian: it says only where you are — in the countryside — and a rural county can live on tourism or a mine and never plant a row, while an agrarian one rests everything on the land.
A farming town goes further than a rural one — the farms matter there; agrarian claims the most, a society whose law, wealth, and seasons are all built on the land.

Farm-based is the plain description: a farm-based economy simply earns most of its money from farms. Agrarian claims far more — a whole social order built on the land, where law, wealth, and the calendar all grow out of who holds and works the soil.

Pastoral is the idealized countryside of poems and paintings — shepherds, meadows, and a soft golden light. Agrarian is the working reality underneath: who plows, who owns the field, who collects the rent. A scene can be pastoral; only a society ordered around farming is agrarian.
